test_title: PYST 17: SSC GD Constable 2022 - English (Held On : 16 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to make it a meaningful sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.

Patients __who do previous heart attacks and those with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having__ a cardiac arrest.

options.text: who have had previous heart attack and they with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having
who have had previous heart attacks and those of cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having
who have had previous heart attacks and those with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having

solution:
The correct answer is **"****who have had previous heart attacks and those with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having ".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb structure in the original sentence, **"who do previous heart attacks", **doesn’t make sense and isn't grammatically correct. A person doesn't 'do' a heart attack.
 
• The phrase should be **"who have had previous heart attacks". **The verb **'have had' **indicates these patients experienced heart attacks in the past.
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence should read: "Patients who have had previous heart attacks and those with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having a cardiac arrest."

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "who have had previous heart attack and they with cardiac failure are at higher risk of having" is incorrect due to the inappropriate use of 'they' which breaks the flow and clarity of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2:** "who have had previous heart attacks and those of cardiac failure are at higher risk of having" is incorrect as the phrase 'those of cardiac failure' doesn't clearly refer to the patients.
